exam_scheme.note: Conducted by the Directorate of Educational Research and Training (DERT), Meghalaya in accordance with the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) guidelines under Section 23(1) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. The examination consists of two separate objective test papers: Paper-I for candidates intending to teach Classes I to V (Lower Primary Stage) and Paper-II for candidates intending to teach Classes VI to VIII (Upper Primary Stage). Each paper comprises 150 multiple-choice questions (150 marks) of 150 minutes (2 hours 30 minutes) duration with no negative marking. The minimum qualifying benchmark is 60% aggregate (90 out of 150 marks) for General category candidates, with a 5% relaxation to 55% (82 out of 150 marks) for SC, ST, OBC, and Differently Abled candidates. Candidates qualifying MTET are awarded a Teacher Eligibility Certificate with lifetime validity.

competition_benchmarks.note: Official candidate appearance, qualification count, and percentage datasets published by the Directorate of Educational Research & Training (DERT), Meghalaya on 03 September 2026 across 24 district examination centres. In accordance with NCTE guidelines, MTET is an eligibility benchmark examination rather than a competitive vacancy-filling test; hence vacancies are not applicable.
